resources.string: A dedicated switch for the sent and read ticks: on shows the shape picked in the list below, off brings back the official Android Telegram ticks. Applies after restarting the app.
The new shape applies after restarting the app.
The exact same thin ticks you already have, completely untouched - the default.
One heart when sent, a pair of hearts when the message is read.
A five-point star when sent, two stars when read.
A simple round dot when sent, two dots when read.
A four-point sparkle when sent, two sparkles when read.
A lightning bolt when sent, two bolts when read.
A crescent moon when sent, two crescents when read.
A diamond when sent, two diamonds when read.

MeeroX is an unofficial Telegram client.

• MeeroX does not collect, store or transmit your personal data to any third party.
• Your messages travel only between your device and Telegram's servers, exactly as with the official app.
• Settings, fonts and preferences are stored locally on your device.
• The source code is open and can be reviewed at any time.

By continuing you agree to use MeeroX at your own responsibility, and to respect Telegram's Terms of Service.
Add a font from your device
That file could not be loaded as a font. Pick a valid .ttf or .otf file.
Frosted glass backdrop when you long-press a message.
Capsule shape with a visible tail. Turn off for stock Telegram bubbles.
Open menu with a single tap
Tap a message bubble to open its menu. Long press keeps working.
New messages spring into place from the corner, the way iOS does.
Group settings rows into inset rounded cards, iOS 26 style.
Centred title, filled folder tabs, pill search field and an always-visible Edit button. Restart to apply everywhere.
Use Telegram for iOS\'s own glyphs. They are static, so the animated tab icons are replaced.
Use Telegram for iOS\'s own send and receive tones.
A hairline outline on menus, panels and the search field.
Thinner ring that stretches as it spins, sized the way Telegram for iOS draws it.
Taller, softly rounded code boxes set in a monospaced face, sized the way Telegram for iOS draws them.
iOS typography and button sizing on the intro pages, with page dots that slide instead of stretching. The animations themselves stay as they are.
Solid tinted pill with a smaller, dimmer magnifier, the way UISearchBar is drawn. Removes the hairline edge.
Lists every section letter down the edge so you can tap straight to one, instead of dragging a handle. Long indexes are thinned to fit.
A wide, faint shadow under settings and profile cards, the way iOS suggests depth instead of drawing an outline.
Distinct feedback for selections, confirmations and errors instead of one buzz for everything. Needs Android 11 or newer for the full set.
A context menu scales up out of the message or row it belongs to, instead of always unfolding from its own corner.
Draws the composer text area as a filled capsule, the way iOS does, with the emoji and attach buttons left outside it.
Wider, fully rounded waveform bars on a 4pt pitch, and a lighter recording indicator, matching Telegram for iOS.
Every MeeroX switch in one place, grouped by what it changes.
Uses Telegram for iOS\'s own glyphs for the pin, mute, archive and delete controls shown while chats are selected, and for the entries in the overflow menu behind them.

Lays a chat row out the way iOS does - a 60dp picture 16dp from the edge with the text starting at 84dp - and applies the same sizing to the account switcher, where it also shows each account\'s unread count.
Groups the collapsed story circles beside the \"Chats\" title and centres the pair the way iOS does, instead of parking them at the left edge, and draws them at the reference size.
Draws the round controls on the call screen at the 72dp Telegram for iOS uses instead of 52, spaces them the way it does, and sets each label at 13dp, 8dp below its button.
Rules a hairline above the buttons of a dialog and between each pair, the way Telegram for iOS separates its alert actions.
Prints a video\'s length straight onto its thumbnail under a soft shadow, as Telegram for iOS does, instead of boxing it in a filled tag.
